newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up 70 bps to 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up 70 bps to 10.4 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 10.4 percent on Wednesday from 9.7 percent the previous day on slightly higher demand and amid improved liquidity.
Daily trade totalled 60 million kuna against 70 million on offer.
Fresh loans accounted for 30.1 million kuna, the majority of it call money granted at a steady rate of 10.5 percent. A one-week loan was granted at nine percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at nine percent for one-week and 12 percent for two-week borrowings.
Banks charged 12 percent for old one-week and 11 percent for one-month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 6.1001 against the dollar and at 3.5786 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
